subject: BetaHealth: audit log export / immutability questions (follow-up)
messages:
From: Linh Tran <linh.tran@betahealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: security@betahealth.com
Date: 2026-02-14T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery call recap - audit logging needs

Thanks for the call this morning, Karthik. Quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying questions before we start the vendor questionnaire: 
- Primary focus: capture admin activity (user changes, role assignments), API request/response logs, and data access events for PHI scopes.
- Retention expectation: 7 years for audit trails (per internal policy), with ability to export on audit request.
- Immutability: we need assurance logs can be exported in a tamper-evident way (WORM or signed exports).

Questions: 
1) Can Redwood provide admin activity logs at a per-user granularity (who, what, prior_value, new_value, timestamp, request_id)?
2) Is there an API or S3 export mechanism for bulk download of logs? Any support for signed/immutable exports?
3) Are there SOC 2 attachments or reports we can start with while we fill the full questionnaire?

I'll attach the high-level vendor questionnaire (we'll send the formal doc) and would like to kick off the security review this week.

Thanks,
Linh Tran
Senior IT Security Manager | BetaHealth

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Linh Tran <linh.tran@betahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-14T17:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery call recap - audit logging needs

Hi Linh — great to sync earlier. Short answers up front, details below and attachments.
- Admin activity: yes, we capture per-user admin events including actor, action, target, before/after where applicable, timestamp, and a request_id that ties to API logs.
- Exports: we support scheduled and on-demand exports to customer S3 buckets (server-side encrypted). We also offer a streaming audit webhook for near-real-time ingestion.
- Immutability: exports can be signed with an envelope hash; we can enable WORM on S3 if you control the bucket. For hosted logs we provide signed manifests with checksums.

Attachments: I attached our SOC 2 summary and a sample audit log schema CSV to help you map fields for your questionnaire.

Next steps proposed: 
1) Linh to share the vendor questionnaire (you mentioned a short one) — we can return answers in 48 business hours.
2) Marissa will coordinate a short technical call to walk through the audit export flow and S3 setup (30 minutes).
3) Vivek will scope the immutability guarantees and provide wording you can use in the questionnaire.

If that works I’ll block times for the tech call tomorrow or Tuesday.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Linh Tran <linh.tran@betahealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-15T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery call recap - audit logging needs

Hi Linh — happy to join a technical walk-through. A couple of practical notes for the questionnaire: 
- Table mapping: We can provide a CSV sample with the most common fields (timestamp, actor_id, actor_email, action_type, resource_type, resource_id, diff_before, diff_after, request_id, ip_address, user_agent). The attached auditlog-sample-schema.csv is a starting point.
- API logs: Stored as separate records with request/response time, status_code, path, model_id, token_count, request_id. These can be correlated to admin events via request_id.
- Export formats: JSONL and Parquet supported. Parquet is recommended for long-term exports/analytics.
- Access controls: export role is restricted to customers' security admins via RBAC and MFA.

Proposed tech call agenda (30 min):
1) Quick architecture overview (5 min)
2) Demo of scheduled export to S3 (10 min)
3) Walkthrough of signed manifest and verification process (10 min)
4) Q&A + next steps (5 min)

Available slots: 2026-02-16 09:00-11:00 PT or 2026-02-17 13:30-15:30 PT. Linh, which works best?

Thanks,
Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Linh Tran <linh.tran@betahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Thanks, Marissa — 2026-02-16 09:30 PT works for us. A couple of clarifications before the call: \n- For immutability: we will need a signed hash that is generated at the time of export and retained with the export manifest.\n- For retention: BetaHealth will keep copies in our own S3 with object lock (WORM) enabled; we just need a cryptographic proof from Redwood that the exported batch matches what you served.\n- For scope: do your audit logs include deletions and anonymization actions (we need to show chain-of-change for PHI redaction steps)?\n
We’ll upload the short vendor questionnaire to the Drive link you provided and flag the fields we expect explicit wording for (e.g., "log immutability", "signed export manifest", "per-user admin events").\n
Linh\n

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Linh Tran <linh.tran@betahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-16T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery call recap - audit logging needs

Linh — thanks and looking forward to the call. Quick engineering notes ahead of tomorrow: 
- Yes, deletions and anonymization actions are recorded as events. For anonymization we include the action type, policy_id (if triggered by an automated policy), prior_value as a hash placeholder, and a redaction marker so you can reconstruct the chain-of-change without exposing PHI in transit.
- Signed export workflow: we produce a JSONL export and a signed manifest file containing SHA256 hashes for each file plus an overall manifest signature (RSA-2048). We can also mirror the manifest signature to a time-stamped log that you can reference during audit.
- Correlation: request_id and actor_id tie admin events to API logs; we also include sequence numbers to detect missing batches.

Deliverables after call (ETA 48 business hours): 
- Completed vendor questionnaire answers (turnaround 48 business hours once you upload).
- Example signed export and verification steps (a step-by-step guide + verification script).
- SOC 2 report redaction-safe summary (we included an engineering-friendly summary attached).

If BetaHealth confirms 09:30 PT we’ll send a calendar invite with the tech-call link and the Drive upload location for the questionnaire.

— Vivek
Principal Engineer, Platform Security | Redwood Inference
